column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“Lip to lip” is rendered “brim to brim,” “round all around” as “circular in form,” and “a measuring-line … went round” as “its circumference.”
“The likeness of oxen” is rendered “figures like oxen.” “Ten by the cubit” is rendered “ten cubits”; the meaning is uncertain. “In its casting” is rendered “in one piece.”
“Turning” is rendered “facing.”
Close to the Hebrew.

“From the south” and “from the left” are rendered “on the right side” and “on the left.” NASB supplies “in which to wash,” and “the work of the burnt offering” is rendered “things for the burnt offering.”
“According to their ordinance” is rendered “in the way prescribed for them.”
“South” and “north” are rendered “right side” and “left.”
“The great precinct” is rendered “the great court.”
NASB supplies “of the house”; “from the side of south eastward” is rendered “on the right side … toward the southeast.”
“Pots” is rendered “pails”; NASB adds “also.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“For the one network” is rendered “for each network.”

Close to the Hebrew.
“Pots” is rendered “pails,” and “their articles” as “its utensils.”
“The valley” is rendered “the plain,” and “the thickness of the ground” as “the clay ground.”
“Ascertained” is rendered “found out.”
NASB adds “even.”
Word order is changed; “according to the ordinance” is rendered “in the way prescribed.”
“Blossom” is rendered “flowers,” and “perfections of gold” as “purest gold.”
“Pans” is rendered “spoons”; NASB supplies “that is,” and “the house of the temple” is rendered “the nave.”
